why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items and neither is broken. Item 1: Check 3 gets the list of exported functions from math.js at the head and fails if "any exported function is not documented in README.md". It also names subtract outright: "At minimum this includes add, subtract, multiply and clamp. Note that subtract was not documented before this change." A README that documents clamp but not subtract would therefore fail. Item 2: no PASS/FAIL condition is stricter than its line. Check 1 compares only the printed return values, and Check 2 only requires `e instanceof RangeError`, with no message text. Check 3 asks for each function by name plus a description, which is what "documents" means, not a layout. Check 4 is exit 0 with no failing tests. The heading style, test coverage and error-message checks are labelled "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)". The layout details in the builder brief are build instructions, not verifier conditions.
